comparator.name: Media and Culture
comparator.academicYear: 2026–27 public curriculum for a Fall 2026 entrant, checked 2026-09-27
comparator.sourceNotes: The official English curriculum supplies 60 EC in each year. Year 1 is a shared media-studies foundation. Year 2 includes three 12-EC restricted-choice groups in which students choose Film Studies or Television and Cross-Media Culture, alongside Global Media Culture, Media Worlds and two philosophy courses. The normalized target names neither route, so the first-listed Film Studies route is selected consistently across all three groups under the neutral official-order rule. Year 3 contains 42 EC of genuine free choice and an 18-EC research seminar and bachelor thesis.

comparatorRouteSelection.basis: The programme requires coherent Film Studies or Television and Cross-Media Culture choices, but the normalized target names neither. Film Studies is the first route listed in the official curriculum and is selected independently of UCR fit.

alternativeSelection.assessment: Three feasible and materially distinct UCR curricula are included: a broad closest match, a Film-led direction and a Television and Cross-Media direction. These cover the official programme structure and stable study directions at the three-alternative maximum.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: Introduction to Film & Media is the closest scheduled UCR counterpart to Living Information, while the programmes retain different curricular structures and production resources.
Media & the Environment is the closest scheduled UCR counterpart to Media and Culture in Transformation, while the programmes retain different curricular structures and production resources.
The Art of Rhetorical Communication is the closest scheduled UCR counterpart to Doing Media Studies 1, while the programmes retain different curricular structures and production resources.
Media Archaeology is the closest scheduled UCR counterpart to Media Theory, while the programmes retain different curricular structures and production resources.
Style & Meaning is the closest scheduled UCR counterpart to Doing Media Studies 2, while the programmes retain different curricular structures and production resources.

The Documentary is the closest scheduled UCR counterpart to Restricted-choice electives: Analysis — Film Studies selected, while the programmes retain different curricular structures and production resources.

Creative Communication Laboratory is the closest scheduled UCR counterpart to Restricted-choice electives: Practices — Film Studies selected, while the programmes retain different curricular structures and production resources.

Media & Race is the closest scheduled UCR counterpart to Advanced Topics in Media and Culture — Film Studies selected, while the programmes retain different curricular structures and production resources.
Introduction to Western Art History is the closest scheduled UCR counterpart to Media Aesthetics, while the programmes retain different curricular structures and production resources.
World Myth & Literature is the closest scheduled UCR counterpart to Current Themes in Media Studies, while the programmes retain different curricular structures and production resources.
Modern History is the closest scheduled UCR counterpart to Global Media Culture, while the programmes retain different curricular structures and production resources.

Introduction to Western Philosophy is the closest scheduled UCR counterpart to Philosophy of the Humanities 1 (Media Studies), while the programmes retain different curricular structures and production resources.
Ethics is the closest scheduled UCR counterpart to Philosophy of the Humanities 2 (Media and Culture), while the programmes retain different curricular structures and production resources.

History Research Seminar is the closest scheduled UCR counterpart to Research Seminar and Bachelor's Thesis Media and Culture, while the programmes retain different curricular structures and production resources.
Qualitative Research Methodology is the closest scheduled UCR counterpart to Media Research, while the programmes retain different curricular structures and production resources.
New Issues in Contemporary Social Theory is the closest scheduled UCR counterpart to Media Worlds, while the programmes retain different curricular structures and production resources.
The 42-EC UvA space is genuinely open choice, so no fixed UCR course is asserted as its counterpart.

notes.text: UvA provides a dedicated Media Studies sequence with explicit Film and Television practice choices. UCR combines related media, communication, literature, visual culture, history, philosophy and social-science courses but does not reproduce UvA production facilities or its compulsory 12-EC practice blocks. The comparison therefore reflects academic direction rather than one-to-one professional production equivalence.
